penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Compliance middleware touching SSO, SCIM provisioning, and audit log pipelines requires significant per-customer setup, configuration, and ongoing validation — not fully automatable via Claude + a simple form.

penalties_applied.name: regulated_industry
penalties_applied.reason: SOC-2 compliance tooling is directly tied to security audit and certification workflows; misdelivery has legal/reputational consequences and buyers expect vendor accountability, increasing support and liability burden.

rationale: The buyer is a real, named person with budget authority — IT/security leads at SMBs paying for SOC-2 audits — and willingness to pay is stated explicitly. However, building a functioning compliance middleware layer for Fastmail (SSO, SCIM, audit log aggregation) requires deep API integration work that goes well beyond Claude + prompts + Stripe, and per-customer onboarding/configuration would be unavoidable. Combined penalties for regulated-industry liability and per-customer manual fulfillment bring the total to 3.0, well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: This is not a viable solo factory build at this time. The core product — a compliance overlay enforcing 2FA, SCIM provisioning, and audit-log aggregation on top of Fastmail's APIs — requires custom OAuth/SAML plumbing, real-time event ingestion, and per-customer configuration that cannot be delivered via Claude prompts alone. Each customer would also need hands-on onboarding to connect their identity provider and validate compliance controls, which breaks the autonomy model entirely. If Fastmail ever exposes richer APIs, this could be revisited as a productized checklist or self-audit report tool — but in its current form it is not buildable or deliverable by a non-technical solo operator.
notes: Failing build gates: buildability_with_ai (4, min 6) and operational_autonomy (4, min 7). Strong pain and WTP signal — worth monitoring if Fastmail releases enterprise APIs or a partner program.
